nodes.name: One-step solution-phase synthesis of M-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of M^{2+} (M = Fe, Co, or Ni)-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 is achieved via a one-step solution-phase method. The Fe-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 sample deposited on Ni foam substrate exhibits a similar nanorod/nanosheet hierarchical structure as that on Cu foam substrate, whereas the Fe-doped sample synthesized without substrate presents uneven nanoparticles.

unit_operations.name: Nucleation and growth
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Ni or Cu foam substrate can supply rough surface for the nucleation and growth of a nanorod/nanosheet hierarchical structure.

nodes.source_text: The synthesis of M2+ (M = Fe, Co, or Ni)-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 is achieved via a one-step solution-phase method... As extending the reaction time to 12 h, the nanosheet is crystallized to orthorhombic SnSe and hexagonal SnSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns reveal mixed crystalline phases of orthorhombic SnSe (JCPDS no. 75-1843) and hexagonal SnSe2 (JCPDS no. 38-1055) for all M2+-doped and undoped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of M2+ (M = Fe, Co, or Ni)-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 and undoped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 reveal they are all the mixed crystalline phases of orthorhombic SnSe (JCPDS no. 75-1843) and hexagonal SnSe2 (JCPDS no. 38-1055) (Figure S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectrum of a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 shows characteristic vibration peaks of SnSe and SnSe2, while M2+-doped samples exhibit red shifts to lower wavenumbers due to defects or tensile strain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum of a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 presents the characteristic vibration peaks of SnSe and SnSe2 (Figure S3), while those of M2+-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 products are all red shifted to lower wavenumbers relative to a/c-SnSe/SnSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX spectra confirm doping amounts of Fe, Co, or Ni are all about 9.0%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDX spectra of the products unveil the doping amount of M (M = Fe, Co, or Ni) are all about 9.0% (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals Fe-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 has nanorod/nanosheet hierarchical structure with nanorods ca. 25 nm diameter, 250 nm length, and nanosheets ca. 12 nm lateral size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM image of Fe-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 in Figure 1a presents it is a nanorod/nanosheet hierarchical structure, in which the nanorods are ca. 25 nm in diameter and 250 nm in length, and the nanosheets are ca. 12 nm in lateral size.

properties.description: Dense fibrillar or nanofiber network morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM verifies nanorod/nanosheet hierarchical structure of Fe-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding TEM image verifies its nanorod/nanosheet hierarchical structure (inset in Figure 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM reveals nanorod/nanosheet hierarchical structure with uniform distribution of Sn, Se, and Fe elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM image of Fe-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 further clearly reveals its nanorod/nanosheet hierarchical structure, and the corresponding elemental mappings showcase the uniform distribution of Sn, Se and Fe elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.287 nm and 0.268 nm for (040) and (121) planes of orthorhombic SnSe, 0.310 nm and 0.261 nm for (002) and (101) planes of hexagonal SnSe2, with amorphous regions and interfacial defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image of Fe9.0%-a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 shows the nanorod is partially covered with thin nanosheets (Figure 1c), where the magnified dotted frame of c1 reveals the lattice spacings are 0.287 and 0.268 nm, which are consistent with (040) and (121) crystal planes of orthorhombic SnSe... the explicit lattice spacings of 0.310 and 0.261 nm... are matched with (002) and (101) crystal planes of hexagonal SnSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Sn 3d shows Sn4+ at 487.3/495.6 eV and Sn2+ at 485.9/494.3 eV; Fe2+ at 710.4/724.3 eV; Co2+ at 781.2/796.3 eV; Ni2+ at 856.1/873.7 eV; Sn 3d peaks positively shifted 0.2 eV (Fe), 0.1 eV (Co), negatively 0.1 eV (Ni); Se 3d negatively shifted.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS spectra are applied to identify the surface composition and electronic structure of M2+ (M = Fe Co, or Ni)-doped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2. As shown in Figure 1d, for a/c-SnSe/SnSe2, the binding energies of Sn 3d at 487.3 and 495.6 eV can be individually ascribed to Sn 3d5/2 and Sn 3d3/2 of Sn4+, while those at 485.9 and 494.3 eV are matched with Sn 3d5/2 and Sn 3d3/2 of Sn2+... Compared to a/c-SnSe/SnSe2, the peaks of Sn 3d are positively shifted 0.2 eV in Fe9.0%-a/c-SnSe/SnSe2, and 0.1 eV in Co9.0%-a/c-SnSe/SnSe2, whereas negatively shifted 0.1 eV in Ni9.0%-a/c-SnSe/SnSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mott-Schottky plots confirm p-n junction formation with both positive (n-type SnSe2) and negative (p-type SnSe) slopes; M2+ doping reduces absolute slopes and increases flat band potentials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of the p-n junction is confirmed by Mott-Schottky (MS) plot that shows both a positive (n-type semiconductor) and a negative (p-type semiconductor) slopes in each catalyst (Figure S30).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR spectra show M2+ doping induces more Se vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra of the catalysts state M2+ ions doping induces more Se vacancies (Figure S31).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS reveals M2+ doping improves conductivity, with Fe-doped catalyst showing best conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) of the catalysts further reveal that M2+ ions doping can remarkably improve the conductivity of a/c-SnSe/SnSe2, of which the catalyst by Fe doping exhibits the best conductivity (Figure S32).

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSAs of M9.0%-a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 show similar increase compared to undoped a/c-SnSe/SnSe2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemically active surface areas (ECSAs) of Fe9.0%-, Co9.0%-, or Ni9.0%-a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 showcase similar increase compared to a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 (Figure S33e).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ DRIFTS on Fe9.0%-a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 shows *COB at 1838 cm⁻¹, *COL at 1911 cm⁻¹, *CO*OH, *OHC*CHO at 1741 cm⁻¹, *CHO at 1470 cm⁻¹, CH3CHO* at 1697 cm⁻¹, *OCH2CH3 at 1339 cm⁻¹ with maximal intensity at -0.6 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Fe9.0%-a/c-SnSe/SnSe2 (Figure 3b), the C=O stretching vibration of *COB appears at 1838 cm⁻¹ at -0.5 V... a new peak at 1911 cm⁻¹ at -0.5 V can be assigned to the C=O stretching mode of the linear *COL... a new band at 1741 cm⁻¹ at -0.4 V features the out-of-phase C=O stretching vibration of *OHC*CHO... The new peak at 1339 cm⁻¹ at -0.5 V is C-H stretching vibration of *OCH2CH3... where the peak intensity reaches the maximal value at -0.6 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey spectra confirm no Cu peak, indicating no copper leaching from Cu foam substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS survey spectra of the catalysts all have no Cu peak (Figure S11), suggesting no copper is leached from Cu foam and incorporated into the catalysts.
